headline: I design systems that *scale* — and the pipelines that *ship* them.
intro: From the first line of code to the last packet through the load balancer, I care about the whole journey: architecture, infrastructure, delivery, and the product people actually use.
chaptersIntro: Every system has an origin story. Here's mine — scroll through it.

chapters.title: It started with a broken website
chapters.body: I taught myself HTML to fix a site nobody else would touch. The moment it loaded, I was hooked — not just on building things, but on understanding why they break.

chapters.title: From pages to products
chapters.body: I moved on to full-stack web and mobile apps: React front ends, Node and Python APIs, Flutter on the phone. Shipping features taught me that great code is useless if it can't reach users reliably.

chapters.title: Falling for the pipeline
chapters.body: Manual deploys at 2 a.m. pushed me into DevOps. I automated everything I could — CI/CD, infrastructure as code, containers — and watched release days go from dreaded to boring. Boring is good.

chapters.title: Thinking in systems
chapters.body: Scale forced bigger questions: queues or streams? SQL or NoSQL? Where do we cache, and what happens when a region goes dark? System design became the way I reason about every problem.

chapters.title: Building on the cloud
chapters.body: Today I architect cloud platforms end to end — secure, observable, cost-aware — and still write the app code that runs on them. I'm looking for teams who want both halves done right.
